name: Algonquin
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Algonquin, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Algonquin, IL: Miracle on Main downtown, Santa at Historic Village Hall, characters at Algonquin Commons and trains nearby.
lede: Algonquin celebrates Christmas on Main Street, where the village lights its tree beside Historic Village Hall and Santa and Mrs. Claus arrive for the evening.
celebrates: The Village of Algonquin hosts Miracle on Main each December along South Main Street in the old downtown, between Route 62 and Madison Street. The village plan for the evening includes the Merry Market, live reindeer, a trackless train, music on two stages, an ice sculptor and a tree lighting on the plaza after Santa and Mrs. Claus arrive. Riverbottom Ice Cream has handed out hot cocoa at the event. Across town, Algonquin Commons on Randall Road runs a Letters to Santa mailbox, and the Algonquin Area Public Library brings local school choirs in for holiday concerts.
lastyear: In 2025 the village flyer showed Miracle on Main was planned for December 6 from 4 to 7 pm, with a Merry Market of more than 20 vendors opening at 3 pm. The plan listed photos with the Grinch, Olaf and Anna, a holiday inflatable, and performers including the Jacobs Dance Team, the Algonquin Middle School Choir and the Dundee Crown D-Chamber Choir. The Northwest Herald also listed the tree lighting, Santa, live reindeer and trackless train.
facts: Algonquin was settled in 1834 and incorporated as a village in 1890. Historic Village Hall, at 2 S. Main Street, was built for $6,848 and designed by Elgin architect William W. Abel with elements of Frank Lloyd Wright's Prairie Style. It first held the sprinkling wagon, the fire department and the jail, and from 1921 the village library. The hall and the Public Square became county landmarks in 1993.
trains: Algonquin has no Metra station of its own. The nearest station is in neighboring Crystal Lake, on the Union Pacific Northwest line. Metra runs decorated Holiday Trains in December, and the UP Northwest line is on the schedule, so check Metra's holiday train page. For a ride with Santa, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs a holiday train, and the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs Santa's Trolley Express.
train_links: The largest railway museum in the US, with holiday train rides each season.

traditions: The village fills South Main Street with a market, music, live reindeer and Santa's arrival each December.
Santa helps light the village tree on the plaza by Historic Village Hall right after he arrives.
Riverbottom Ice Cream at Washington and Main has handed out hot cocoa to the first families at Miracle on Main.
Algonquin Commons sets up a Santa mailbox in the Café at The Fresh Market, with weekly gift card drawings.
High school choirs from Dundee Crown and Jacobs sing at the Algonquin Area Public Library.
The Rotary Club of Algonquin has photo albums of its Breakfast with Santa going back to 2012.
kidfact: Algonquin's old Village Hall once kept a sprinkling wagon on its first floor. Workers used it to spray water on the dirt roads so they would not be so dusty.
faq: When is Miracle on Main in Algonquin?

Miracle on Main is the Village of Algonquin's holiday evening on South Main Street, held on a Saturday in early December. In 2025 it was planned for December 6 from 4 to 7 pm, with the Merry Market opening at 3 pm. Check the village Miracle on Main page for this year's schedule, parking and the time Santa arrives.
Where do you park for Miracle on Main?

The village parking list for Miracle on Main includes Towne Park at 100 Jefferson Street, St. John's Lutheran Church at 300 Jefferson Street, and street parking on Washington Street, Jefferson Street and La Fox River Drive. Restrooms are in Historic Village Hall and on Washington Street near the bank. Arrive early, since the village says to allow time to find a spot before Santa arrives.
Is there a sensory friendly Santa in Algonquin?

Yes. The Village of Algonquin Recreation Department offers Sensory Friendly Photos with Santa and Mrs. Claus at Historic Village Hall, in private 10 minute sessions with reduced stimulation for people of all abilities. It is offered with HLC Therapy and Mindful Minis Photos. Pre-registration is required, and there is a small fee per family.
Where can kids mail a letter to Santa in Algonquin?

Algonquin Commons runs Letters to Santa with a mailbox in the Café at The Fresh Market. Blank letters are at The Fresh Market, V's Barbershop, Hallmark and Mr. Kimichi, and a weekly drawing awards a $25 gift card. At Miracle on Main, kids have also written letters at Bella Vita Salon, and Santa writes back.
What is Historic Village Hall in Algonquin?

Historic Village Hall at 2 S. Main Street was Algonquin's first village hall, finished in early 1907. Over the years it held the fire department, the jail, the council chambers and, from 1921, the village library. Village offices moved to Harnish Drive in 1996, and the old hall was restored. It is the center of Miracle on Main.
